Fluorescein can detect Seidel sign indicative of globe rupture. Pressure should not be applied to the eye until globe rupture is ruled out.
ExplanationAR: إصابة عين من انفجار: تقييم بصبغة الفلوريسين (fluorescein) للبحث عن Seidel sign (دليل على تمزق المقلة). يُمنع الضغط على العين قبل استبعاد globe rupture.
ClinicalScenario: A 15-year-old boy after a bombing at a train station with right eye pain. What is the best next step in the management of his eye pain?

Question: A 33-year-old man with chest pain 4 hours after MVC. Sternal tenderness, ECG not yet done, chest x-ray without acute injuries, bedside cardiac US normal. What is the best next study to obtain?
ExplanationEN: Chest pain in blunt thoracic trauma should raise suspicion for cardiac contusion. An ECG is an essential component of the workup for cardiac contusion to screen for arrhythmias, ST abnormalities, or new bundle-branch blocks.
ExplanationAR: ألم صدري بعد رضح صدري كليل: يُشتبه بضربة القلب (cardiac contusion). تخطيط القلب (ECG) هو أول فحص للكشف عن اضطرابات النظم أو تغيرات ST أو حصار فرع حزمة جديد.
ClinicalScenario: A 33-year-old man with chest pain 4 hours after MVC. Sternal tenderness, ECG not yet done, chest x-ray without acute injuries, bedside cardiac US normal. What is the best next study to obtain?

Question: A 33-year-old man with chest pain after MVC. Bedside cardiac US normal. ECG shows RBBB, no prior ECG available. What part of the heart is most likely to be injured?
ExplanationEN: Nonspecific ECG changes are the most common in cardiac contusion. RBBB is most consistent with an injury to the right ventricle. Because of its anterior position in the chest and close proximity to the sternum, the right ventricle is the most frequently injured part of the heart in cardiac contusion.
ExplanationAR: ضربة القلب: البطين الأيمن (RV) هو الأكثر إصابة بسبب موقعه الأمامي القريب من القص. الحصار الفرع الأيمن (RBBB) على ECG يوحي بإصابة RV.
ClinicalScenario: A 33-year-old man with chest pain after MVC. Bedside cardiac US normal. ECG shows RBBB, no prior ECG available. What part of the heart is most likely to be injured?

Question: A 33-year-old man with chest pain 4 hours after MVC, ECG shows RBBB. What is the best next diagnostic evaluation?
ExplanationEN: Troponin I is highly specific to myocardial injury. A normal troponin I with a normal ECG is a strong indicator for the absence of cardiac injury. CK-MB has low sensitivity and specificity. Standard echocardiography cannot detect minor myocardial injury.
ExplanationAR: التروبونين I (troponin I) هو الأكثر حساسية ونوعية لاستبعاد ضربة القلب. المستوى الطبيعي مع ECG طبيعي ينفي إصابة قلبية سريرية. CK-MB أقل حساسية، والإيكو لا يكتشف الإصابة العضلية الدقيقة.
ClinicalScenario: A 33-year-old man with chest pain 4 hours after MVC, ECG shows RBBB. What is the best next diagnostic evaluation?

Question: A 17-year-old boy found unconscious with a sheet wrapped around his neck, on backboard with C-collar. Awake, alert, midline tenderness posteriorly, normal neuro exam. Which feature is an indication for imaging of the cervical spine?
ExplanationEN: This patient would fail the NEXUS criteria due to midline tenderness and would fail the CCR due to lack of any low-risk factors (simple rear-end MVC, ambulatory, seated in ED, delayed onset of neck pain, absence of midline tenderness). Further workup with CT is indicated.
ExplanationAR: حساسية خط المنتصف على الفحص (midline tenderness) هي الاستطباب لتصوير العمود الرقبي. المريض يفشل معايير NEXUS وقاعدة كندا للعمود الرقبي (CCR).
ClinicalScenario: A 17-year-old boy found unconscious with a sheet wrapped around his neck, on backboard with C-collar. Awake, alert, midline tenderness posteriorly, normal neuro exam. Which feature is an indication for imaging of the cervical spine?

Question: A 17-year-old boy after strangulation with C4 transverse process fracture extending through the transverse foramen. Which additional diagnostic test is indicated?
ExplanationEN: Fractures at the transverse foramen can be associated with blunt cerebrovascular injuries (BCVI) due to the course of the vertebral arteries. The expanded Denver screening criteria recommend CTA of the neck in the setting of any identified cervical spine fracture.
ExplanationAR: كسر النتوء المستعرض في الفقرة الرقبية قد يترافق مع إصابة وعائية دماغية كليلة (BCVI) بسبب مرور الشريان الفقري. CTA للرقبة مطلوب حسب معايير Denver الموسعة.
ClinicalScenario: A 17-year-old boy after strangulation with C4 transverse process fracture extending through the transverse foramen. Which additional diagnostic test is indicated?

Question: A 17-year-old boy with C4 transverse process fracture, after observation develops bilateral shoulder numbness and weakness of grip in both hands. What is the most likely diagnosis?
ExplanationEN: Central cord syndrome is the most common traumatic spinal cord syndrome. It occurs with hyperextension of the neck causing injury and edema to the central corticospinal tract. Characterized by loss of motor/sensory function bilaterally, disproportionately affecting upper extremities (cape-like).
ExplanationAR: متلازمة الحبل المركزي (central cord syndrome): الأكثر شيوعًا بعد رضح رقبي فرط البسط. تُصيب الأطراف العلوية أكثر من السفلية (نمط كابي). يتم التشخيص بـ MRI.
ClinicalScenario: A 17-year-old boy with C4 transverse process fracture, after observation develops bilateral shoulder numbness and weakness of grip in both hands. What is the most likely diagnosis?

Question: An 18-year-old man after assault with stab wound and swelling at right sternoclavicular junction, pale, dysphonia, BP 60/palp. What is the best initial approach for airway management?

Options.text: Intubation only if there is respiratory failure or complete airway obstruction
Rapid sequence induction (RSI) with a sedative and paralytic

CorrectAnswer: Rapid sequence induction (RSI) with a sedative and paralytic
ExplanationEN: Impending respiratory failure with dysphonia (hard sign) warrants aggressive airway management. RSI is standard. Cricothyrotomy is reserved for 'can't intubate, can't ventilate'. Awake intubation is less likely to succeed in a moving, agitated, peri-arrest patient.
ExplanationAR: فشل تنفسي وشيك مع بحة صوت (dysphonia) في رضح رقبي نافذ: RSI هو النهج الأمثل للتنبيب الفوري. لا يُبدأ بـ cricothyrotomy أو awake intubation في مريض غير مستقر.
ClinicalScenario: An 18-year-old man after assault with stab wound and swelling at right sternoclavicular junction, pale, dysphonia, BP 60/palp. What is the best initial approach for airway management?

Question: An 18-year-old man with stab wound to sternoclavicular junction in extremis. What method of hemorrhage control is contraindicated?

Options.text: Internal pressure applied with finger, gauze, or Foley catheter
Thoracotomy in the case of cardiac arrest in the emergency department
Zone I resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta inflation

CorrectAnswer: Zone I resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta inflation
ExplanationEN: Zone I REBOA describes descending aorta balloon placement between the left subclavian artery and the celiac trunk. It is contraindicated in cases of thoracic hemorrhage or pericardial tamponade because it cannot control ongoing blood loss from a major vessel breach in the thoracic outlet.
ExplanationAR: الـ REBOA في المنطقة I ممنوع في النزف الصدري أو اندساس التامور لأنه لا يسيطر على نزف من وعاء كبير في المخرج الصدري. يُستخدم فقط في النزف تحت الحجاب.
ClinicalScenario: An 18-year-old man with stab wound to sternoclavicular junction in extremis. What method of hemorrhage control is contraindicated?

Question: An 18-year-old man with stab wound to sternoclavicular junction. After resuscitation with blood products, still hypotensive, expanding hematoma continues to bleed briskly when pressure released. What is the best next step?
ExplanationEN: Expanding hematoma from penetrating neck wound with hard signs of vascular injury (brisk bleeding, hemorrhagic shock, expansile/pulsatile hematoma) is an indication for emergent surgical exploration. CT angiography is for stable patients with soft signs.
ExplanationAR: ورم دموي متوسع مع نزف غزير مستمر من رضح رقبي نافذ = علامات وعائية صلبة (hard signs) → استكشاف جراحي طارئ. CTA محجوز للمرضى المستقرين.
ClinicalScenario: An 18-year-old man with stab wound to sternoclavicular junction. After resuscitation with blood products, still hypotensive, expanding hematoma continues to bleed briskly when pressure released. What is the best next step?

Question: A 24-year-old woman after being pushed down stairs by boyfriend. Which component of history most increases her risk for becoming a victim of completed intimate partner homicide?
ExplanationEN: The greatest risk factor for intimate partner homicide (IPH) in a relationship with previous IPV is the perpetrator having access to firearms. Risk increases eleven-fold if abuser has access to firearms. Other factors: prior nonfatal strangulation, pregnancy, race, perpetrator alcohol use.
ExplanationAR: وجود سلاح ناري في المنزل (gun in the home) هو أقوى عامل خطر لقتل الشريك الحميم (IPH)، خصوصًا مع تاريخ عنف سابق. يزيد الخطر ~11 ضعفًا.
ClinicalScenario: A 24-year-old woman after being pushed down stairs by boyfriend. Which component of history most increases her risk for becoming a victim of completed intimate partner homicide?

Question: A 24-year-old woman after attempted strangulation by boyfriend, denies LOC/dyspnea, petechiae of face, normal neuro exam. What diagnostic test should be ordered?
ExplanationEN: Blunt neck trauma from strangulation can cause internal injuries in the absence of external trauma. Petechiae indicate extravasation of blood. CTA of the neck is the study of choice for assessing vascular injuries with high sensitivity and specificity. Must include base of skull vessels.
ExplanationAR: خنق (strangulation): النمشات الوجهية (petechiae) تدل على رضح وعائي. CTA للرقبة هو الفحص المفضل لتقييم BCVI بحساسية ونوعية عاليتين.
ClinicalScenario: A 24-year-old woman after attempted strangulation by boyfriend, denies LOC/dyspnea, petechiae of face, normal neuro exam. What diagnostic test should be ordered?

Question: A 24-year-old woman after attempted strangulation with CTA showing right vertebral artery dissection. What is the best next step?

Options.text: Admit the patient on heparin IV
Admit the patient on tPA IV
Discharge the patient on apixaban PO
Discharge the patient on aspirin PO

CorrectAnswer: Admit the patient on heparin IV
ExplanationEN: Acute vertebral artery dissection without stroke should be admitted for neurological monitoring, with greatest stroke risk within 72 hours. Antithrombotic therapy with heparin should be initiated. There is no indication for tPA without acute stroke symptoms.
ExplanationAR: تسلخ الشريان الفقري (vertebral artery dissection): إدخال للمراقبة العصبية + هيبارين وريدي لتقليل خطر الجلطة خلال 72 ساعة. لا حاجة لـ tPA بدون سكتة حادة.
ClinicalScenario: A 24-year-old woman after attempted strangulation with CTA showing right vertebral artery dissection. What is the best next step?

Question: An obese 14-year-old boy with 3 weeks of intermittent right hip pain, worse after practice, limps. What is the preferred imaging study?

Options.text: Anteroposterior and lateral x-rays of the pelvis
Anteroposterior and lateral x-rays of the right hip
CT scan of the right hip

CorrectAnswer: Anteroposterior and lateral x-rays of the pelvis
ExplanationEN: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE) in an obese adolescent boy with hip pain. Plain x-rays are preferred. Bilateral hip imaging with AP and lateral pelvis x-rays is best given high incidence of bilateral disease. Frog-leg lateral risk further displacement.
ExplanationAR: انزلاق مشاشة رأس الفخذ (SCFE) في مراهق بدين: تصوير الحوض AP + lateral (كلا الوركين). وضعية الضفدع (frog-leg) ممنوعة لأنها قد تزيد الانزياح.
ClinicalScenario: An obese 14-year-old boy with 3 weeks of intermittent right hip pain, worse after practice, limps. What is the preferred imaging study?

Question: A 14-year-old obese boy after a tackle develops acute hip pain. X-ray shows posterior hip dislocation. Which statement is true?

Options.text: Delay in management may result in avascular necrosis
It is an indication for placement of a hare traction splint
The extremity is usually externally rotated, flexed, and abducted

CorrectAnswer: Delay in management may result in avascular necrosis
ExplanationEN: Posterior hip dislocation in pediatric population. Disruption of vascular supply to the femoral head can result in avascular necrosis; likelihood greatly increases with delays in reduction beyond 6 hours. Hip dislocations should be urgently reduced in the ED.
ExplanationAR: خلع الورك الخلفي (posterior hip dislocation): تأخير الإرجاع >6 ساعات يزيد خطر التنخر الوعائي (avascular necrosis). يجب الإرجاع العاجل في الطوارئ (ليس fixation جراحي).
ClinicalScenario: A 14-year-old obese boy after a tackle develops acute hip pain. X-ray shows posterior hip dislocation. Which statement is true?

Question: An obese 14-year-old boy after high-speed MVC, BP 85/55, pelvic x-ray shows open-book pelvic fracture. What is the most important initial treatment?
ExplanationEN: Anterior-posterior compression fracture (open-book) of the pelvis. Pelvic binder placement reduces pubic symphysis diastasis, reducing pelvic volume and space for hemorrhage. Must be correctly placed at the level of greater trochanters.
ExplanationAR: كسر الحوض من النوع الأمامي-الخلفي (open-book): يوضع حزام الحوض على مستوى المدورين الكبيرين لتقليل حجم الحوض وفراغ النزف. يُطبّق قبل نقل الدم.
ClinicalScenario: An obese 14-year-old boy after high-speed MVC, BP 85/55, pelvic x-ray shows open-book pelvic fracture. What is the most important initial treatment?

Question: A 56-year-old man with history of AAA repair presents with abdominal pain, N/V, lightheadedness, hematemesis, BP 85/55, P 130. Abdomen with well-healed midline scar, diffuse tenderness, frank blood on rectal. What is the best next step?

Options.text: Obtain a kidney, ureter, and bladder x-ray
Obtain an MRA of the abdomen and pelvis

ExplanationEN: Secondary aortoenteric fistula after AAA repair. Patient is hemodynamically unstable and requires early surgical consultation and emergent laparotomy. Massive transfusion is appropriate. Endoscopy is inappropriate in an unstable patient with suspected aortoenteric fistula.
ExplanationAR: ناسور أبهر-معوي ثانوي (secondary aortoenteric fistula) بعد إصلاح أم الدم الأبهرية: نزف هضمي + صدمة. يتطلب استشارة جراحية ولاباروتومي عاجل. لا تنظير في مريض غير مستقر.
ClinicalScenario: A 56-year-old man with history of AAA repair presents with abdominal pain, N/V, lightheadedness, hematemesis, BP 85/55, P 130. Abdomen with well-healed midline scar, diffuse tenderness, frank blood on rectal. What is the best next step?

Question: A 56-year-old man with ulcerative colitis, BP 85/55, abdominal distension, tenderness. Upright abdominal x-ray shows colonic dilation with absent haustra. What is the most likely diagnosis?
ExplanationEN: Toxic megacolon is nonobstructive dilation of the colon with signs of systemic toxicity. Usually associated with inflammatory bowel disease, especially ulcerative colitis. AXR shows colonic dilation >6 cm with absent/abnormal haustra. Indication for surgery.
ExplanationAR: القولون السمي (toxic megacolon): توسع قولوني غير انسدادي >6 سم مع غياب/شذوذ الحويسرات (haustra) + علامات تسمم جهازي. يرتبط بـ UC ويُعد استطبابًا جراحيًا.
ClinicalScenario: A 56-year-old man with ulcerative colitis, BP 85/55, abdominal distension, tenderness. Upright abdominal x-ray shows colonic dilation with absent haustra. What is the most likely diagnosis?

Question: A 56-year-old man with a plastic shampoo bottle in his rectum and unable to remove it. Upright chest x-ray shows free air under the diaphragm. What is the best next step?

Options.text: Attempt bedside removal of the bottle
CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis

ExplanationEN: Rectal foreign body with free air under the diaphragm confirms perforation. Emergent surgical consultation is necessary. Transrectal removal in the ED is contraindicated with perforation. CT delay would be inappropriate.
ExplanationAR: جسم غريب شرجي مع هواء حر تحت الحجاب = انثقاب (rectal perforation). استشارة جراحية فورية ضرورية. لا محاولة إخراج في الطوارئ.
ClinicalScenario: A 56-year-old man with a plastic shampoo bottle in his rectum and unable to remove it. Upright chest x-ray shows free air under the diaphragm. What is the best next step?

Question: A 22-year-old man with GSW to abdomen, BP 78/52, P 138, confused, FAST positive. What is the next most appropriate step?

Options.text: Rapid infusion of 2 L of lactated Ringer solution
Transfusion of one unit of packed RBCs

ExplanationEN: Hemorrhagic shock with ABC score ≥2 (penetrating torso, SBP<90, HR>120, positive FAST). Massive transfusion protocol involves pre-specified amounts and ratios of universal donor blood products. Crystalloid resuscitation worsens coagulopathy.
ExplanationAR: صدمة نزفية مع ABC score ≥2 (رضح نافذ، SBP<90، HR>120، FAST موجب): يُبدأ بروتوكول نقل الدم الضخم (MTP) فورًا. السوائل البلورية تضر بالتخثر.
ClinicalScenario: A 22-year-old man with GSW to abdomen, BP 78/52, P 138, confused, FAST positive. What is the next most appropriate step?

Question: A 22-year-old man with MVC, BP 78/52, P 138, confused, FAST negative. After 2 units pRBC no improvement. What is the next most appropriate intervention?

Options.text: Transfusion of one additional unit of packed RBCs
Transfusion of one pack of apheresis platelets
Transfusion of one unit of fresh frozen plasma

CorrectAnswer: Transfusion of one unit of fresh frozen plasma
ExplanationEN: Hemorrhagic shock. Excessive pRBC administration can cause dilutional coagulopathy. Balanced resuscitation should follow a 1:1:1 or 1:1:2 ratio of plasma:platelets:RBCs. Given 2 pRBC already given, next is FFP. Vasopressors are not indicated in hemorrhagic shock.
ExplanationAR: في نقل الدم الضخم: يجب الحفاظ على نسبة متوازنة 1:1:1 أو 1:1:2 من بلازما:صفيحات:كريات حمر. بعد وحدتين pRBC، يُعطى FFP لتجنب اعتلال التخثر بالتخفيف.
ClinicalScenario: A 22-year-old man with MVC, BP 78/52, P 138, confused, FAST negative. After 2 units pRBC no improvement. What is the next most appropriate intervention?

Question: A 22-year-old man after MVC. After 6 units pRBC, 6 units FFP, and apheresis platelets over 30 minutes, what laboratory value may be helpful in guiding further treatment?
ExplanationEN: Stored blood is anticoagulated with citrate, which binds ionized calcium. Massive transfusion overwhelms the liver's ability to clear citrate, causing hypocalcemia with further hypotension and dysrhythmias. Ionized calcium should be frequently measured and repleted to >4.4 mg/dL.
ExplanationAR: نقل الدم الضخم: السيترات (citrate) في الدم المخزّن ترتبط بالكالسيوم المتأين مسببة نقص كالسيوم (hypocalcemia) → هبوط ضغط واضطرابات نظم. يجب مراقبة الكالسيوم المتأين وإعطاء الكالسيوم بعد 4-6 وحدات.
ClinicalScenario: A 22-year-old man after MVC. After 6 units pRBC, 6 units FFP, and apheresis platelets over 30 minutes, what laboratory value may be helpful in guiding further treatment?

Question: A 36-year-old pregnant woman after high-speed MVC, unresponsive and intubated, uterine fundus 4 cm above umbilicus, BP 75/55. What is the optimal positioning?
ExplanationEN: After 20 weeks' gestation, pregnant patients placed supine are at risk of aortocaval compression syndrome. The best positioning is to tilt the backboard 15° to 30° to the left, or to manually displace the uterus to the left.
ExplanationAR: حامل >20 أسبوعًا: الوضع المستلقي (supine) يسبب متلازمة انضغاط الأبهر والوريد الأجوف (aortocaval compression). الأفضل هو الإمالة الجانبية اليسرى (left lateral tilt) 15-30°.
ClinicalScenario: A 36-year-old pregnant woman after high-speed MVC, unresponsive and intubated, uterine fundus 4 cm above umbilicus, BP 75/55. What is the optimal positioning?

Question: A 36-year-old pregnant woman after MVC, eFAST shows anechoic stripe in Morison pouch, fetal HR 180. What is the best next step?
ExplanationEN: Presumed hemorrhagic shock with positive FAST. Continue resuscitation with blood transfusion. O– blood is preferred for women of childbearing age to prevent Rh alloimmunization. Resuscitating the mother is the best treatment for the fetal tachycardia at this time.
ExplanationAR: في صدمة نزفية مع FAST موجب لحامل: نقل دم O- هو الأفضل (لمنع تحصس Rh). إنعاش الأم هو العلاج الأفضل لتسرع قلب الجنين. لا vasopressors (تُقلل التروية المشيمية).
ClinicalScenario: A 36-year-old pregnant woman after MVC, eFAST shows anechoic stripe in Morison pouch, fetal HR 180. What is the best next step?

Question: A 36-year-old pregnant woman after MVC, eFAST shows intra-abdominal fluid. She develops PEA arrest. After 1 round ACLS and 2 units pRBC, remains in PEA. What is the best next step in resuscitation?
ExplanationEN: Cardiac arrest in a pregnant patient with uterine fundus at or above the umbilicus (gestational age ≥20 weeks). Removing the metabolic demands of the fetus may improve the mother's hemodynamics. Procedure should be started within 4 minutes of arrest, delivery within 5 minutes.
ExplanationAR: توقف قلب في حامل مع قاع رحم فوق السرة (≥20 أسبوعًا): يُجرى بضع الرحم الإنعاشي (resuscitative hysterotomy) خلال 4-5 دقائق لإزالة الحمل وتحسين ديناميكا الأم.
ClinicalScenario: A 36-year-old pregnant woman after MVC, eFAST shows intra-abdominal fluid. She develops PEA arrest. After 1 round ACLS and 2 units pRBC, remains in PEA. What is the best next step in resuscitation?

Question: A 15-year-old girl with 3 days of heavy vaginal bleeding and clots, mild cramping, LMP 3 weeks ago. What is the most appropriate next step?
ExplanationEN: Abnormal uterine bleeding in a reproductive-age female. The next step is to determine the patient's pregnancy status; causes and management differ significantly in pregnant vs nonpregnant patients. Five major causes of early pregnancy bleeding include ectopic, spontaneous abortion, threatened abortion, implantation, and cervical/vaginal/uterine pathologies.
ExplanationAR: نزف رحمي غير طبيعي في سن الإنجاب: أول خطوة هي اختبار الحمل (pregnancy test) لأن الأسباب والتدبير تختلف تمامًا بين الحامل وغير الحامل.
ClinicalScenario: A 15-year-old girl with 3 days of heavy vaginal bleeding and clots, mild cramping, LMP 3 weeks ago. What is the most appropriate next step?

Question: A 15-year-old premenarchal girl with Down syndrome, not sexually active, presents with 5 days of intermittent vaginal bleeding and foul-smelling discharge. Nontender abdomen. What is the most likely cause?
ExplanationEN: A vaginal foreign body is the most likely diagnosis in girls who present with vaginal bleeding and no history of trauma. Vaginal bleeding with or without discharge is the most common symptom in prepubertal girls with vaginal foreign bodies. Bleeding is typically light, spotty, or intermittent.
ExplanationAR: جسم غريب مهبلي (retained vaginal foreign body): السبب الأرجح في طفلة قبل البلوغ مع نزف مهبلي وإفراز كريه بدون رضح. النزف عادةً بسيط ومتقطع.
ClinicalScenario: A 15-year-old premenarchal girl with Down syndrome, not sexually active, presents with 5 days of intermittent vaginal bleeding and foul-smelling discharge. Nontender abdomen. What is the most likely cause?

Question: A 15-year-old girl with 2 days of bright red vaginal bleeding without clot, no abdominal pain, firm uterus with fundus above umbilicus. Which diagnostic approach is the best next step?
ExplanationEN: Likely placenta previa given uterine size. Placenta previa refers to placental tissue extending over the internal cervical os. It should be suspected with painless vaginal bleeding after 20 weeks' gestation. Ultrasound should be performed before any digital vaginal exam to avoid severe hemorrhage.
ExplanationAR: المشيمة المنزاحة (placenta previa): نزف مهبلي غير مؤلم بعد 20 أسبوعًا. الإيكو عبر البطن (transabdominal) أولًا قبل أي فحص مهبلي رقمي لأن لمس المشيمة يُسبب نزفًا شديدًا.
ClinicalScenario: A 15-year-old girl with 2 days of bright red vaginal bleeding without clot, no abdominal pain, firm uterus with fundus above umbilicus. Which diagnostic approach is the best next step?

Question: An otherwise healthy 32-year-old woman has just given birth in the ED. After delivery of placenta, she has continued bleeding of 1,500 cc. Uterus feels boggy. What is the first medication that should be administered?
ExplanationEN: Postpartum hemorrhage. Uterine atony is the etiology in 70-80% of cases. Oxytocin is the first-line medication per ACOG, administered as 10-40 units in 1L NS IV over 30-60 minutes. Fundal massage should also be used.
ExplanationAR: نزف ما بعد الولادة (postpartum hemorrhage): السبب الأكثر شيوعًا هو وهن الرحم (uterine atony) 70-80%. العلاج الأول هو الأوكسيتوسين (oxytocin) 10-40 وحدة في 1L NS + تدليك الرحم.
ClinicalScenario: An otherwise healthy 32-year-old woman has just given birth in the ED. After delivery of placenta, she has continued bleeding of 1,500 cc. Uterus feels boggy. What is the first medication that should be administered?

Question: A 32-year-old woman postpartum continues to bleed despite uterotonics. After 2 units pRBC, what other medication should be given to help with ongoing bleeding?
ExplanationEN: After uterotonics and MTP, tranexamic acid (TXA) 1 g IV inhibits fibrinolysis and can abate bleeding. The WOMAN trial demonstrated TXA in postpartum hemorrhage reduces risk of death from bleeding.
ExplanationAR: نزف ما بعد الولادة المستمر: حمض الترانيكساميك (TXA) 1 g وريدي يثبط انحلال الفيبرين ويقلل النزف. أثبتت تجربة WOMAN انخفاض الوفيات النزفية.
ClinicalScenario: A 32-year-old woman postpartum continues to bleed despite uterotonics. After 2 units pRBC, what other medication should be given to help with ongoing bleeding?

Question: A 32-year-old woman postpartum with ongoing bleeding despite uterotonics, MTP, and TXA. No uterine inversion, no lacerations, no retained placenta. What is the best option to tamponade the ongoing uterine bleeding?
ExplanationEN: The Bakri balloon is specifically made for uterine tamponade in postpartum hemorrhage. The catheter is placed through the cervical canal into the uterus. The balloon is inflated with up to 500 mL of sterile saline.
ExplanationAR: بالون باكري (Bakri balloon) هو الجهاز المخصص للسيطرة على نزف الرحم في نزف ما بعد الولادة: يُنفخ حتى 500 mL محلول ملحي لتطويق النزف.
ClinicalScenario: A 32-year-old woman postpartum with ongoing bleeding despite uterotonics, MTP, and TXA. No uterine inversion, no lacerations, no retained placenta. What is the best option to tamponade the ongoing uterine bleeding?

Question: A 60-year-old man with stage II CKD and hypertension, presents with fever and productive cough for 3 days. Vital signs normal except T 38.2°C. Labs: BUN 18, Na 136, WBC 12,000. CXR shows infiltrate. What is the most appropriate disposition?
ExplanationEN: Multiple studies evaluated which patients with community-acquired pneumonia are appropriate for discharge home. Two validated decision rules are the Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI/PORT) and CURB-65. This patient's scores under both suggest outpatient management is appropriate. Clinical judgment supersedes decision tools.
ExplanationAR: ذات الرئة المكتسبة (CAP) منخفضة الخطورة حسب PSI/CURB-65 → إخراج للمنزل مع مضادات حيوية فموية. إدخال ICU فقط مع حاجة للرافعات الوعائية أو التهوية الميكانيكية (معايير IDSA/ATS للـ severe CAP).
ClinicalScenario: A 60-year-old man with stage II CKD and hypertension, presents with fever and productive cough for 3 days. Vital signs normal except T 38.2°C. Labs: BUN 18, Na 136, WBC 12,000. CXR shows infiltrate. What is the most appropriate disposition?

Question: A 55-year-old man with CAD risk factors has sudden chest pain, collapses, receives dispatcher CPR. Fire department performs CPR, epinephrine, defibrillation with ROSC. Intubated. What should be done after achieving ROSC?
ExplanationEN: One of the most important components of post-resuscitation care is determining whether or not a STEMI was the cause of the cardiac arrest. Performing an ECG after ROSC allows for rapid recognition of a STEMI. Treatment should be with PCI or thrombolytics.
ExplanationAR: بعد استعادة الدورة (ROSC): يجب عمل ECG فورًا لتحديد STEMI كسبب للتوقف القلبي. إن وُجد STEMI → PCI أو حالات التخثر. لا تُستخدم beta-blockers أو lidocaine روتينيًا.
ClinicalScenario: A 55-year-old man with CAD risk factors has sudden chest pain, collapses, receives dispatcher CPR. Fire department performs CPR, epinephrine, defibrillation with ROSC. Intubated. What should be done after achieving ROSC?

Question: A 31-year-old man with ulcerative colitis presents with left wrist pain after a fall. X-rays show no fracture. Placed in thumb spica splint. What is the most appropriate outpatient pain regimen?
ExplanationEN: This patient likely has a wrist sprain or occult scaphoid fracture. Splinting, acetaminophen, and NSAIDs are typically all that are needed. The ACEP clinical policy on opioids recommends that nonopioid pain medications be prescribed from the ED for initial treatment of acute pain.
ExplanationAR: التواء الرسغ أو كسر زورقي كامن (occult scaphoid fracture): الأكثر أمانًا هو acetaminophen + NSAIDs. لا تُوصف الأفيونات (opioids) روتينيًا في الطوارئ للألم الحاد حسب سياسة ACEP.
ClinicalScenario: A 31-year-old man with ulcerative colitis presents with left wrist pain after a fall. X-rays show no fracture. Placed in thumb spica splint. What is the most appropriate outpatient pain regimen?

Question: A woman at 41 weeks' gestation delivers a baby. Almost 2 minutes after delivery, the newborn's heart rate is 85 bpm. What is the next step?

Options.text: Warm the infant and reassess in 1 minute

ExplanationEN: Neonatal resuscitation. At 60 seconds after birth, if the infant is apneic, hypoventilatory, or has a heart rate between 60 and 100 bpm, positive-pressure ventilation with a BVM should be initiated. Chest compressions are for HR <60 bpm.
ExplanationAR: إنعاش حديثي الولادة: HR 60-100 بعد دقيقة → تهوية بالضغط الموجب (PPV) بالقناع. ضغطات الصدر للحالات HR <60 فقط. الأدرينالين إذا استمر <60 بعد التهوية والضغطات.
ClinicalScenario: A woman at 41 weeks' gestation delivers a baby. Almost 2 minutes after delivery, the newborn's heart rate is 85 bpm. What is the next step?

Question: A 13-day-old infant presents with a fever. Which factor portends the most increased risk of neonatal sepsis in this patient?

Options.text: Group B Streptococcus with intrapartum antibiotics

ExplanationEN: Fever in the neonatal period is concerning for neonatal sepsis. Risk factors include prematurity <37 weeks, chorioamnionitis, maternal fever, active maternal HSV or genital lesions, and complicated postpartum course. GBS colonization risk is reduced with intrapartum antibiotics.
ExplanationAR: حمى الوليد → إنتان محتمل. أقوى عامل خطر هو التهاب السلى والمشيمة الحموي (chorioamnionitis). GBS يُخفف خطرها بالمضادات الحيوية أثناء المخاض.
ClinicalScenario: A 13-day-old infant presents with a fever. Which factor portends the most increased risk of neonatal sepsis in this patient?

Question: A 27-year-old woman at 24 weeks' gestation with new elevated BP 150/95, no proteinuria, normal labs. What is the most appropriate treatment of her hypertension?
ExplanationEN: Gestational hypertension is hypertension after the 20th week of pregnancy or immediately postpartum without preexisting hypertension. Differentiated from preeclampsia by absence of proteinuria or systemic abnormalities. First-line therapy is labetalol or nifedipine. ACE inhibitors and ARBs are contraindicated.
ExplanationAR: ارتفاع ضغط الحمل (gestational hypertension): العلاج الأول هو labetalol أو nifedipine. مثبطات ACE (lisinopril) وحاصرات مستقبلات الأنجيوتنسين (valsartan) ممنوعة في الحمل.
ClinicalScenario: A 27-year-old woman at 24 weeks' gestation with new elevated BP 150/95, no proteinuria, normal labs. What is the most appropriate treatment of her hypertension?

Question: A 40-year-old man with pleuritic chest pain 2 weeks after COVID-19. CT shows subsegmental PE without right heart strain. What is the best treatment strategy?

Options.text: Admit to hospital on enoxaparin SQ
Admit to hospital on heparin IV

ExplanationEN: Low-risk PE can be discharged on oral anticoagulation. The Hestia criteria and simplified PESI score help determine appropriateness. DOACs (apixaban, rivaroxaban) are first-line for uncomplicated VTE. This patient meets criteria for outpatient management.
ExplanationAR: PE منخفض الخطورة حسب Hestia/sPESI: يُخرج على مضاد تخثر فموي مباشر (apixaban). DOACs هي الخط الأول للـ VTE غير المعقد.
ClinicalScenario: A 40-year-old man with pleuritic chest pain 2 weeks after COVID-19. CT shows subsegmental PE without right heart strain. What is the best treatment strategy?

Question: According to ACLS updates 2018 and 2019, which medication should be considered after 1 mg IV epinephrine every 5 minutes for a patient in cardiac arrest?
ExplanationEN: According to the 2019 ACLS update, vasopressin has been added back as an additional therapy to be considered (Class 2b), but not to replace epinephrine. High-dose epinephrine, magnesium, and beta-blockers are not recommended.
ExplanationAR: تحديث ACLS 2019: يمكن اعتبار vasopressin كعلاج إضافي بعد epinephrine (Class 2b) لكنه لا يستبدله. لا يُنصح بـ high-dose epinephrine أو المغنيزيوم أو حاصرات بيتا في التوقف القلبي.
ClinicalScenario: According to ACLS updates 2018 and 2019, which medication should be considered after 1 mg IV epinephrine every 5 minutes for a patient in cardiac arrest?

Question: According to ACEP's 2020 Clinical Policy on opioids, what is the best initial treatment for a patient who presents in acute opioid withdrawal?
ExplanationEN: According to the 2020 ACEP Clinical Policy on opioids, buprenorphine is the most effective therapy to treat acute withdrawal symptoms. Preferentially treat opioid withdrawal in the ED with buprenorphine rather than methadone. COWS score >8 indicates buprenorphine administration.
ExplanationAR: انسحاب الأفيونات الحاد: buprenorphine هو العلاج المفضل (يفضّل على methadone). يُعطى عند COWS >8. يعمل كـ partial agonist على مستقبلات mu.
ClinicalScenario: According to ACEP's 2020 Clinical Policy on opioids, what is the best initial treatment for a patient who presents in acute opioid withdrawal?

Question: According to the 2019 AHA focused update on PALS, what is the recommended airway management for pediatric patients in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest?
ExplanationEN: According to the 2019 AHA update on PALS, BVM ventilation should be continued in pediatric patients in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Advanced airways do not improve survival or neurologic outcomes. Consider advanced airway only if BVM is unsuccessful.
ExplanationAR: PALS 2019: في التوقف القلبي خارج المستشفى عند الأطفال، يُستمر في تهوية القناع (BVM). المسالك المتقدمة (ETT/SGA) لا تُحسن البقاء أو النتائج العصبية.
ClinicalScenario: According to the 2019 AHA focused update on PALS, what is the recommended airway management for pediatric patients in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest?

Question: According to the ACEP Clinical Policy on acute headaches and the Ottawa SAH Rule, what indicates the need to obtain neuroimaging for SAH in a patient with acute headache?
ExplanationEN: Ottawa SAH Rule can rule out SAH in neurologically intact patients. Cannot rule out if any of: age >40, neck pain/stiffness, loss of consciousness, thunderclap headache, limited neck flexion, onset during exertion. Only one criterion needed for neuroimaging.
ExplanationAR: قاعدة أوتاوا للنزف تحت العنكبوتية: LOC هو أحد المعايير التي تستدعي التصوير. معايير أخرى: عمر >40، ألم/تصلب رقبي، صداع رعدي، محدودية انثناء الرقبة، بدء أثناء الجهد.
ClinicalScenario: According to the ACEP Clinical Policy on acute headaches and the Ottawa SAH Rule, what indicates the need to obtain neuroimaging for SAH in a patient with acute headache?

Question: A 67-year-old man with history of MRSA, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, productive cough for 3 days. Which laboratory test should be obtained to tailor empiric therapy?
ExplanationEN: IDSA/ATS recommend MRSA nasal PCR or culture for any patient with history of MRSA or when MRSA treatment is being started empirically. The HCAP category no longer exists. If empiric coverage for MRSA is given, PCR or culture data should be obtained.
ExplanationAR: CAP مع تاريخ MRSA: يجب الحصول على MRSA nasal PCR لتوجيه العلاج التجريبي. إن بدأ تغطية MRSA (vancomycin) فيجب الحصول على PCR/ثقافة لإمكانية التعديل.
ClinicalScenario: A 67-year-old man with history of MRSA, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, productive cough for 3 days. Which laboratory test should be obtained to tailor empiric therapy?

Question: A 55-year-old man with cardiac arrest on dispatcher CPR. What medication should be administered next?
ExplanationEN: Standard-dose epinephrine (1 mg every 3-5 minutes) is the only medication strongly recommended by the AHA in cardiac arrest. Atropine is no longer recommended in cardiac arrest. High-dose epinephrine has not shown benefit.
ExplanationAR: في التوقف القلبي: epinephrine بالجرعة القياسية (1 mg كل 3-5 دقائق) هو العلاج الوحيد الذي توصي به AHA بقوة. الأتروبين لم يُعد موصى به، والجرعات العالية غير مفيدة.
ClinicalScenario: A 55-year-old man with cardiac arrest on dispatcher CPR. What medication should be administered next?

Question: A 36-year-old woman with headache and nausea, started at rest 12 hours ago, gradual worsening over first hour. No syncope, LOC, or neck pain/stiffness. Normal neuro exam. Ibuprofen and acetaminophen do not relieve. What is the best next step?

Options.text: Brain MRI with and without contrast
CT angiography of the head and neck
Noncontrast CT scan of the brain

ExplanationEN: Ottawa SAH Clinical Decision Tool: this patient meets all criteria to rule out SAH based on history and physical exam alone. Answering no to age ≥40, neck pain/stiffness, witnessed LOC, onset during exertion, thunderclap headache, and limited neck flexion. 100% sensitive.
ExplanationAR: قاعدة أوتاوا للنزف تحت العنكبوتية: جميع المعايير سلبية → لا حاجة لتصوير. القاعدة حساسة 100% لاستبعاد SAH.
ClinicalScenario: A 36-year-old woman with headache and nausea, started at rest 12 hours ago, gradual worsening over first hour. No syncope, LOC, or neck pain/stiffness. Normal neuro exam. Ibuprofen and acetaminophen do not relieve. What is the best next step?

Question: A 36-year-old woman with headache that started at rest, gradual worsening, no red flags. Ibuprofen and acetaminophen do not relieve. What is the best treatment for this patient's pain?
ExplanationEN: Prochlorperazine and metoclopramide are antiemetics that, when combined with diphenhydramine, show a high rate of success in the treatment of acute headache. ALTO (alternatives to opioids) should be the modality of choice. Opioids increase risk of medication misuse and progression to chronic migraine.
ExplanationAR: صداع حاد: يُفضل بدائل الأفيونات (ALTO) مثل prochlorperazine + diphenhydramine + NSAIDs. الأفيونات والباربيتورات تزيد خطر الإدمان والصداع المزمن.
ClinicalScenario: A 36-year-old woman with headache that started at rest, gradual worsening, no red flags. Ibuprofen and acetaminophen do not relieve. What is the best treatment for this patient's pain?

Question: A 26-year-old woman with body aches, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, piloerection, 3 days after stopping oxycodone. What medication should be administered?
ExplanationEN: Opioid withdrawal after stopping chronic oxycodone. ACEP Clinical Policy on Opioids recommends opioid withdrawal in the ED be treated with buprenorphine or methadone rather than non-opioid-based management. Buprenorphine is preferred over methadone.
ExplanationAR: انسحاب الأفيونات بعد إيقاف الأوكسيكودون المزمن: buprenorphine هو المفضل (partial mu agonist) على methadone. يعالج الانسحاب ويُبقي على العلاج الدوائي المساعد.
ClinicalScenario: A 26-year-old woman with body aches, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, piloerection, 3 days after stopping oxycodone. What medication should be administered?

Question: A 7-year-old girl with UTI on antibiotics, worsening, PEA cardiac arrest at rural hospital. EMT can bag-mask ventilate. What intervention should be prioritized?
ExplanationEN: Likely cardiac arrest from septic shock due to UTI, resulting in hypovolemia and vasoplegia. First-line treatment is crystalloid fluid bolus (20 mL/kg in pediatrics). Can repeat up to 60 mL/kg.
ExplanationAR: توقف قلبي من صدمة إنتانية (septic shock) من UTI: العلاج الأول هو محلول بلوري (20 mL/kg) للأطفال. يمكن تكراره حتى 60 mL/kg.
ClinicalScenario: A 7-year-old girl with UTI on antibiotics, worsening, PEA cardiac arrest at rural hospital. EMT can bag-mask ventilate. What intervention should be prioritized?

Question: A 7-year-old girl post-ROSC remains comatose after septic shock cardiac arrest. Broad-spectrum antibiotics given. What should be prioritized for post-ROSC care?
ExplanationEN: According to the AHA 2019 focused update on PALS, patients who remain comatose after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest should undergo targeted temperature management. Starting range either 32-34°C or 36-37.5°C with continuous core temperature measurement.
ExplanationAR: بعد ROSC في الأطفال مع غياب الوعي: التدبير الحراري الموجّه (TTM) بمدى 32-34°C أو 36-37.5°C مع قياس حرارة مركزية مستمرة. لا بيكربونات روتينية.
ClinicalScenario: A 7-year-old girl post-ROSC remains comatose after septic shock cardiac arrest. Broad-spectrum antibiotics given. What should be prioritized for post-ROSC care?

Question: An academic ED that primarily cares for adults with pediatric hospital nearby. How should this ED best prepare to care for pediatric patients?

Options.text: Hire a pediatric hospitalist to care for all pediatric patients
Limit staff education on pediatric management
Review pediatric treatment protocols every 10 years

ExplanationEN: The National Pediatric Readiness Project (PRP) ensures all hospitals that care for children are ready to provide high-quality pediatric emergency care. 70% of pediatric visits take place at EDs with few pediatric patients. Focus on staff education, protocols, and pediatric-dosed medications/equipment.
ExplanationAR: مشروع الجهوزية لطب الأطفال (PRP): يجب أن تحتفظ كل أقسام الطوارئ بعربة طوارئ أطفال (pediatric crash cart) وأدوية بجرعات الأطفال + تدريب الموظفين. مراجعة البروتوكولات سنويًا.
ClinicalScenario: An academic ED that primarily cares for adults with pediatric hospital nearby. How should this ED best prepare to care for pediatric patients?

Question: A 56-year-old man with hypertension and diabetes presents with shortness of breath, BP 180/110, crackles. What is most likely seen on bedside ultrasound?
ExplanationEN: Acute congestive heart failure (CHF). Sonographic B-lines are hyperechoic reverberating lines indicating thickening of interlobular septa (pulmonary edema). Diffuse bilateral B-lines strongly suggest pulmonary edema. Other findings: IVC collapse <50% and EPSS >7 mm.
ExplanationAR: فشل قلب حاد على الإيكو: B-lines ثنائية منتشرة (دليل وذمة رئوية). علامات أخرى: انخبار IVC أقل من 50%، EPSS >7 mm (كفاءة انقباضية منخفضة).
ClinicalScenario: A 56-year-old man with hypertension and diabetes presents with shortness of breath, BP 180/110, crackles. What is most likely seen on bedside ultrasound?

Question: A 25-year-old man with unknown medical history presents with acute agitation. Verbal deescalation unsuccessful, tries to punch a security guard. What pharmacotherapy is most appropriate?
ExplanationEN: After failed verbal deescalation, physical and chemical restraint is appropriate. For unknown medical history, preferred first-line is antipsychotic + benzodiazepine IM. IM is preferred when no IV access. Consider underlying causes: hypoglycemia, electrolytes, CNS, hypoxia.
ExplanationAR: هياج حاد فشل فيه التهدئة اللفظية: يُعطى مضاد ذهان + بنزوديازيبين عضليًا (droperidol IM + midazolam IM) لأن الوصول الوريدي صعب في مريض عنيف.
ClinicalScenario: A 25-year-old man with unknown medical history presents with acute agitation. Verbal deescalation unsuccessful, tries to punch a security guard. What pharmacotherapy is most appropriate?

Question: A 25-kg, 5-year-old boy with acute respiratory distress from bronchiolitis, hypoxic to 85%, RR 46 despite albuterol. What would be the next most appropriate treatment?
ExplanationEN: Bronchiolitis (usually RSV). HFNC improves clinical course and reduces hospital stay compared to low-flow oxygen. Starting flow rate 1-2 L/kg/min, FiO2 21-30%. Early use of HFNC can prevent the need for more aggressive interventions.
ExplanationAR: التهاب القصيبات (bronchiolitis) مع نقص أكسجة مستمر: HFNC هو الخيار التالي (1-2 L/kg/min). يقلل جهد التنفس ويوفر PEEP خفيف ويقي من التنبيب.
ClinicalScenario: A 25-kg, 5-year-old boy with acute respiratory distress from bronchiolitis, hypoxic to 85%, RR 46 despite albuterol. What would be the next most appropriate treatment?

Question: A patient presents in diabetic ketoacidosis. Glucose 650 mg/dL, potassium 3.8 mEq/L. What is the most appropriate next step?

Options.text: Insulin infusion plus maintenance lactated Ringer solution
Insulin infusion plus maintenance normal saline with 20 mEq/L potassium
Potassium infusion to a goal of >4.0 mEq/L before starting insulin

CorrectAnswer: Insulin infusion plus maintenance normal saline with 20 mEq/L potassium
ExplanationEN: DKA. Mainstay is fluid resuscitation and IV insulin. If K is 3.5-5.0 mEq/L, insulin may be started but maintenance IV fluids (NS or LR) with 20-30 mEq/L of potassium should be given simultaneously to keep serum K around 4 mEq/L. If K <3.5, replace before insulin.
ExplanationAR: الحماض الكيتوني السكري (DKA) مع بوتاسيوم 3.8: يُبدأ الأنسولين مع سوائل صيانة (NS) مضاف إليها 20-30 mEq/L بوتاسيوم للحفاظ على K ~4. لا يُبدأ الأنسولين إذا K <3.5 قبل التعويض.
ClinicalScenario: A patient presents in diabetic ketoacidosis. Glucose 650 mg/dL, potassium 3.8 mEq/L. What is the most appropriate next step?

Question: A patient with opioid withdrawal is given buprenorphine. What is the mechanism of action of buprenorphine?
ExplanationEN: Buprenorphine is a partial mu opioid receptor agonist used to treat opioid withdrawal symptoms. Partial binding abates withdrawal symptoms without causing an acute 'high' (unlike full agonists like heroin). Frequently formulated with naloxone to discourage IV injection.
ExplanationAR: buprenorphine هو ناهض جزئي لمستقبلات الأفيون mu (partial mu agonist): يخفف الانسحاب دون إحداث نشوة كاملة مثل الهيروين. يُدمج مع naloxone لمنع سوء الاستخدام الوريدي.
ClinicalScenario: A patient with opioid withdrawal is given buprenorphine. What is the mechanism of action of buprenorphine?

Question: A patient presents with severe sepsis. Based on CMS core measures, which finding meets the definition of septic shock?

Options.text: BP 70/50 after 30 mL/kg of lactated Ringer
Lactate >2 mmol/L after 20 mL/kg of normal saline
Lactate >3 mmol/L prior to any fluid administration
P >120 bpm after 1 L of normal saline

CorrectAnswer: BP 70/50 after 30 mL/kg of lactated Ringer
ExplanationEN: CMS defines septic shock as severe sepsis plus persistent hypotension after 30 mL/kg crystalloid resuscitation OR lactate ≥4 mmol/L. CMS criteria must be met for reimbursement. Lactate >2 but <4 is 'severe sepsis' not 'septic shock'.
ExplanationAR: CMS: الصدمة الإنتانية = هبوط ضغط مستمر بعد 30 mL/kg محلول بلوري، أو لاكتات ≥4 mmol/L. لاكتات >2 ولكن <4 = إنتان شديد وليس صدمة إنتانية.
ClinicalScenario: A patient presents with severe sepsis. Based on CMS core measures, which finding meets the definition of septic shock?

Question: A minimally responsive patient with right flank bruise. RUSH examination shows free fluid between kidney and liver. What is the best interpretation?

Options.text: Right upper quadrant intraperitoneal free fluid

CorrectAnswer: Right upper quadrant intraperitoneal free fluid
ExplanationEN: RUSH shows free fluid in Morison's pouch (between kidney and liver) in the right upper quadrant. RUSH evaluates cardiac, IVC, lung, abdomen, aorta, DVT. Free fluid in RUQ with flank bruising suggests intra-abdominal bleeding.
ExplanationAR: فحص RUSH: سائل حر في جيب موريسون (Morison's pouch) في الربع العلوي الأيمن = نزف داخل الصفاق. مع كدمة الجنبة = دليل على نزف داخل البطن.
ClinicalScenario: A minimally responsive patient with right flank bruise. RUSH examination shows free fluid between kidney and liver. What is the best interpretation?

Question: In which case of acute asthma exacerbation should a chest x-ray be obtained?

Options.text: 6-year-old with no fever and moderate wheezing improved after two albuterol/ipratropium nebulizers
14-year-old with SpO2 88% improved to 98% with slower RR after albuterol
22-year-old with persistent hypoxia and tachypnea after three albuterol nebulizer treatments
40-year-old with scant wheezing on initial presentation and now asymptomatic after albuterol

CorrectAnswer: 22-year-old with persistent hypoxia and tachypnea after three albuterol nebulizer treatments
ExplanationEN: Chest x-rays are not routinely indicated for acute asthma exacerbations, particularly in pediatric patients. A chest x-ray should be obtained when there is concern for other pathologies (pneumonia, pneumothorax) or if the patient is not improving with initial interventions.
ExplanationAR: لا تُطلب صور الصدر روتينيًا في نوبة الربو. تُطلب فقط عند عدم التحسن مع العلاج الأولي أو الاشتباه بمضاعفات (ذات الرئة، استرواح الصدر).
ClinicalScenario: In which case of acute asthma exacerbation should a chest x-ray be obtained?

Question: A 7-year-old boy undergoing procedural sedation with ketamine develops stridor concerning for laryngospasm and desaturates. What is the next best management step?

Options.text: Continue with the reduction as laryngospasm will resolve spontaneously
Perform positive-pressure ventilation while applying pressure to the Larson point

CorrectAnswer: Perform positive-pressure ventilation while applying pressure to the Larson point
ExplanationEN: If a patient develops laryngospasm, stop the procedure immediately. First step: apply positive-pressure ventilation while providing pressure at the Larson point (base of skull between mastoid and mandibular condyle). Most cases resolve with this. If not, deepen sedation (propofol). If still refractory, paralyze and intubate.
ExplanationAR: تشنج الحنجرة (laryngospasm) بعد التهدئة الإجرائية: التهوية بالضغط الموجب (PPV) + ضغط نقطة Larson (قاعدة الجمجمة بين الخشاء ونتوء الفك) هو الخط الأول. إن استمر: تعميق التهدئة ثم التحلل العضلي والتنبيب.
ClinicalScenario: A 7-year-old boy undergoing procedural sedation with ketamine develops stridor concerning for laryngospasm and desaturates. What is the next best management step?

Question: A 64-year-old man awakens with right-sided arm/leg weakness, facial droop, and aphasia. Last known well 2 am, presented at 8 am. NIHSS 15, CTA shows MCA thrombus. What is the most appropriate next step?

Options.text: Administer aspirin and admit to neurology
Consult neurointerventional radiology for a mechanical thrombectomy

CorrectAnswer: Consult neurointerventional radiology for a mechanical thrombectomy
ExplanationEN: This patient meets criteria for mechanical thrombectomy within 6 hours of symptom onset (mRS 0-1, large-vessel occlusion, NIHSS ≥6, no hemorrhage, ASPECTS ≥6). Also meets DAWN criteria for 6-24 hours. Outside 4.5-hour window for IV tPA.
ExplanationAR: سكتة إسكيمية مع انسداد وعاء كبير (MCA) و NIHSS ≥6 وبداية منذ >4.5 ساعات: الاستئصال الميكانيكي (mechanical thrombectomy) هو العلاج، وليس tPA.
ClinicalScenario: A 64-year-old man awakens with right-sided arm/leg weakness, facial droop, and aphasia. Last known well 2 am, presented at 8 am. NIHSS 15, CTA shows MCA thrombus. What is the most appropriate next step?

Question: A 77-year-old man on a blood thinner that does not require lab checks, presents obtunded with subdural hematoma and 5 mm midline shift. What is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy for reversal?

Options.text: Andexanet alfa and 4-factor prothrombin complex concentrate

ExplanationEN: Life-threatening bleeding with unknown anticoagulant that does not require lab monitoring. Treat with 4-factor PCC. Specific reversal agents (idarucizumab for dabigatran, andexanet alfa for Xa inhibitors) are preferred if drug is known and available.
ExplanationAR: نزف مهدد للحياة مع مضاد تخثر غير معروف (لا يحتاج مراقبة مخبرية): 4-factor PCC هو العلاج التجريبي. إن كان الدواء معروفًا، يُستخدم العامل العكسي المحدد.
ClinicalScenario: A 77-year-old man on a blood thinner that does not require lab checks, presents obtunded with subdural hematoma and 5 mm midline shift. What is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy for reversal?

Question: A 77-year-old man on rivaroxaban after craniotomy recovery, presents 10 months later with epistaxis, Hgb 12.1 (prior 12.3). What is the most appropriate course of management?
ExplanationEN: Minor bleeding (nosebleed, easily controlled) in the setting of DOAC use. Routine care plus holding the next dose is recommended. Reversal agents are not needed for minor bleeding. Restart anticoagulation after resolution.
ExplanationAR: نزف بسيط (epistaxis) على DOAC: أوقف الجرعة التالية مؤقتًا (hold) + رعاية موضعية. لا تُستخدم عوامل العكس (andexanet) إلا في النزف المهدد للحياة أو الموضع الحرج.
ClinicalScenario: A 77-year-old man on rivaroxaban after craniotomy recovery, presents 10 months later with epistaxis, Hgb 12.1 (prior 12.3). What is the most appropriate course of management?

Question: A 45-year-old diabetic woman with COVID-19, SpO2 85% on 4 L NC, accessory muscle use, CXR diffuse inflammatory changes. What is the most appropriate next step to improve oxygenation?

Options.text: Increase the nasal cannula flow rate to 6 L/min
Replace the simple nasal cannula with HFNC

CorrectAnswer: Replace the simple nasal cannula with HFNC
ExplanationEN: COVID-19 respiratory failure is primarily oxygenation failure. HFNC delivers up to 100% FiO2 and flows up to 60 L/min with small PEEP, and can reduce need for intubation. First-line noninvasive therapy for isolated hypoxemic respiratory failure.
ExplanationAR: فشل تنفسي نقص أكسجة من COVID-19: HFNC هو الخط الأول (تدفق حتى 60 L/min، FiO2 حتى 100%، PEEP 1-4 سم ماء). NIPPV محجوز لـ COPD/فرط الكابنيا.
ClinicalScenario: A 45-year-old diabetic woman with COVID-19, SpO2 85% on 4 L NC, accessory muscle use, CXR diffuse inflammatory changes. What is the most appropriate next step to improve oxygenation?

Question: A 45-year-old woman with SOB, increased work of breathing, SpO2 88%, ABG: pH 7.40, PaO2 70, PaCO2 35 (hypoxemic, nonhypercapnic). After nasal cannula at 6 L/min, no improvement. What is the best next step?

Options.text: Apply face mask at flush rate

ExplanationEN: HFNC significantly improves work of breathing, respiratory rate, and oxygenation in primarily hypoxemic respiratory failure. Lower mortality compared to face masks and NIPPV in hypoxemic patients. NIPPV remains first-line for COPD/hypercapnic respiratory failure.
ExplanationAR: فشل تنفسي نقص أكسجة (hypoxemic nonhypercapnic) لا يتحسن بـ NC: HFNC هو الخيار الأول. أظهرت الدراسات انخفاض الوفيات مقارنة بـ NIPPV في هذه الحالة.
ClinicalScenario: A 45-year-old woman with SOB, increased work of breathing, SpO2 88%, ABG: pH 7.40, PaO2 70, PaCO2 35 (hypoxemic, nonhypercapnic). After nasal cannula at 6 L/min, no improvement. What is the best next step?

Question: A 75-year-old man with chronic AF presents with tachycardia, cough, fever, BP 105/64, P 140, T 38.9°C. What is the most appropriate management of this patient's heart rate?

Options.text: Administer diltiazem IV bolus followed by continuous diltiazem infusion
Initiate sepsis care with IV lactated Ringer solution and antibiotics
Perform a synchronized cardioversion with 100 J
Provide procainamide IV followed by intravenous normal saline

CorrectAnswer: Initiate sepsis care with IV lactated Ringer solution and antibiotics
ExplanationEN: This is secondary atrial fibrillation with RVR due to sepsis. Treating with diltiazem could worsen hypotension by preventing the compensatory response. Treat the underlying cause (sepsis) first.
ExplanationAR: رجفان أذيني ثانوي لعدوى (sepsis-induced AF): العلاج هو معالجة الإنتان (سوائل + مضادات حيوية)، وليس diltiazem الذي يُفاقم الهبوط. لا تقويم كهربائي في حال الاستقرار النسبي.
ClinicalScenario: A 75-year-old man with chronic AF presents with tachycardia, cough, fever, BP 105/64, P 140, T 38.9°C. What is the most appropriate management of this patient's heart rate?

Question: A 5-year-old with status epilepticus. Two doses of lorazepam ineffective. What medication should be administered next?
ExplanationEN: Status epilepticus after 2 benzodiazepine doses. Second-line agents include phenytoin/fosphenytoin, levetiracetam, valproic acid, phenobarbital. Additional benzodiazepines are ineffective and increase respiratory depression risk.
ExplanationAR: حالة صرعية (status epilepticus) بعد جرعتين بنزوديازيبين: يُنتقل للخط الثاني (levetiracetam، phenytoin، valproate، phenobarbital). جرعة ثالثة بنزوديازيبين غير فعالة وتزيد خطر تثبيط التنفس.
ClinicalScenario: A 5-year-old with status epilepticus. Two doses of lorazepam ineffective. What medication should be administered next?

Question: Procedural sedation on a 65-year-old. Repeated sternal rubbing required to elicit any response, transient hypopnea and airway obstruction managed with BVM and jaw thrust. HR and BP normal. What level of sedation does this represent?
ExplanationEN: Deep sedation occurs when the patient requires repeated painful stimulation to cause any response. Spontaneous breathing and airway patency may be transiently compromised. Minimal = anxiolysis; moderate = responds to verbal/painful stimuli; general = unresponsive even to painful stimuli.
ExplanationAR: تهدئة عميقة (deep sedation): استجابة فقط للمنبهات المؤلمة المتكررة مع احتمال اضطراب مؤقت في التنفس والمجرى الهوائي. لا يفقد الاستجابة الكاملة كما في التخدير العام.
ClinicalScenario: Procedural sedation on a 65-year-old. Repeated sternal rubbing required to elicit any response, transient hypopnea and airway obstruction managed with BVM and jaw thrust. HR and BP normal. What level of sedation does this represent?

Question: A 70-year-old man with untreated HTN, altered, lactate 5.1. Which additional element of history or exam would suggest benefit from fluid resuscitation and serial lactate checks?
ExplanationEN: Hypothermia and flank pain may point to the source of sepsis (pyelonephritis) responsible for lactatemia. The patient would benefit from fluid bolus and antibiotics. Lactate is a suitable surrogate for perfusion and need for resuscitation.
ExplanationAR: حمى + ألم في الخاصرة = التهاب حويضة وكلية (pyelonephritis) → إنتان قد يستفيد من السوائل والمضادات والمتابعة المتسلسلة للاكتات. اللاكتات المرتفعة تدل على نقص تروية الأنسجة.
ClinicalScenario: A 70-year-old man with untreated HTN, altered, lactate 5.1. Which additional element of history or exam would suggest benefit from fluid resuscitation and serial lactate checks?

Question: A 56-year-old woman with flu-like symptoms, several family members have similar symptoms, cluster indoors in cold weather. Lactate 3.4, VBG pH 7.22. Which additional laboratory test is essential?
ExplanationEN: Family cluster indoors in cold weather = possible carbon monoxide poisoning. Elevated lactate from cellular hypoxia. CO poisoning can cause hypotension, falsely normal SpO2, and neurologic symptoms. Essential to test carboxyhemoglobin.
ExplanationAR: تسمم بأول أكسيد الكربون (CO poisoning): عائلة في مكان مغلق بجو بارد + حماض لبني. SpO2 يبدو طبيعيًا كاذبًا. الفحص الأساسي هو carboxyhemoglobin.
ClinicalScenario: A 56-year-old woman with flu-like symptoms, several family members have similar symptoms, cluster indoors in cold weather. Lactate 3.4, VBG pH 7.22. Which additional laboratory test is essential?

Question: A morbidly obese patient with COPD exacerbation and worsening mental status despite NIPPV. Decision for RSI. Which strategy should be used to facilitate intubation?
ExplanationEN: Morbidly obese patients have difficult intubation due to increased soft tissue and reduced pulmonary reserve. Video laryngoscopy (VL) improves first-pass intubation success. Hyperangulated blade provides better visualization of glottic opening with less soft-tissue manipulation.
ExplanationAR: مريض بدين مع مسلك هوائي صعب متوقع: التنظير بالفيديو (video laryngoscopy) مع نصل شديد التقوس (hyperangulated blade) هو الأفضل لتحسين الرؤية وتقليل مناورة الأنسجة الرخوة.
ClinicalScenario: A morbidly obese patient with COPD exacerbation and worsening mental status despite NIPPV. Decision for RSI. Which strategy should be used to facilitate intubation?

Question: A 62-year-old woman with chest pain, HEART score 2. ECG, CBC, chemistry, chest x-ray, troponin, D-dimer all normal. What is the most appropriate management?

Options.text: Admit for observation and serial troponin levels
Consult cardiology for exercise stress testing
Discharge home with primary care physician follow-up
Order a CT scan of the chest to evaluate for a pulmonary embolism

CorrectAnswer: Discharge home with primary care physician follow-up
ExplanationEN: HEART score is a tool used to risk stratify chest pain patients. Low HEART score (0-3) indicates low short-term risk of major adverse cardiac events (<2.5%) and can be discharged with follow-up.
ExplanationAR: ألم صدري مع HEART score منخفض (0-3): خطر الأحداث القلبية الكبرى خلال 30-45 يومًا منخفض جدًا (<2.5%). يمكن إخراج المريض مع متابعة طبيب الأسرة.
ClinicalScenario: A 62-year-old woman with chest pain, HEART score 2. ECG, CBC, chemistry, chest x-ray, troponin, D-dimer all normal. What is the most appropriate management?

Question: A 20-year-old woman with tick bite noted after a hike in New York 48 hours ago. What further management is needed after removal?

Options.text: Administer a single 200-mg dose of doxycycline to prevent Lyme disease
Administer a single dose of amoxicillin 500 mg
Prescribe doxycycline 100 mg twice a day for 14 days

CorrectAnswer: Administer a single 200-mg dose of doxycycline to prevent Lyme disease
ExplanationEN: A single dose of doxycycline 200 mg can prevent Lyme disease if given within 72 hours of tick removal in endemic areas with deer tick identified and attached >36 hours. Amoxicillin is ineffective for prophylaxis.
ExplanationAR: قرصة قراد في منطقة موبوءة + قراد متغذٍّ >36 ساعة: جرعة واحدة وقائية من doxycycline 200 mg خلال 72 ساعة تمنع داء لايم. الأموكسيسيلين غير فعال للوقاية.
ClinicalScenario: A 20-year-old woman with tick bite noted after a hike in New York 48 hours ago. What further management is needed after removal?

Question: A 28-year-old man with epilepsy presents with status epilepticus. After 8 mg lorazepam IV, seizure continues. What is the appropriate next treatment?
ExplanationEN: Status epilepticus is a seizure lasting >5 minutes or intermittent without return to baseline. After adequate benzodiazepine dosing, IV antiepileptics include phenytoin, fosphenytoin, valproate, levetiracetam, propofol, or barbiturates. Valproate dosing for status: 20-30 mg/kg.
ExplanationAR: حالة صرعية (status epilepticus) بعد جرعة كافية من بنزوديازيبين: يُعطى الخط الثاني وريديًا (valproate 20-30 mg/kg، levetiracetam، phenytoin). لا جرعات إضافية من بنزوديازيبين.
ClinicalScenario: A 28-year-old man with epilepsy presents with status epilepticus. After 8 mg lorazepam IV, seizure continues. What is the appropriate next treatment?

Question: A 50-year-old woman after camping in Portland, Maine. Fever, chills, lymphadenopathy, fatigue, myalgias, headache, rash (targetoid). What is the best next step in risk stratification of this patient?
ExplanationEN: Lyme disease with erythema migrans. An ECG will allow risk stratification of Lyme carditis (mild: first-degree AV block with PR <300 ms; severe: PR ≥300 ms, second- or third-degree block). Symptomatic patients with severe findings require hospitalization and IV antibiotics.
ExplanationAR: داء لايم مع حمامى مهاجرة (erythema migrans): يجب عمل ECG لتقييم التهاب القلب اللايمي (Lyme carditis) — حصار AV من الدرجة الأولى أو الأعلى. الحالات الشديدة (PR ≥300 ms أو حصار من الدرجة الثانية/الثالثة) تتطلب إدخالًا ومضادات وريدية.
ClinicalScenario: A 50-year-old woman after camping in Portland, Maine. Fever, chills, lymphadenopathy, fatigue, myalgias, headache, rash (targetoid). What is the best next step in risk stratification of this patient?

Question: A 61-year-old woman with HTN, T2DM, depression presents with 2 hours of substernal chest pressure. ECG unremarkable, troponin elevated. Concern for NSTEMI. Which intervention is no longer recommended in the initial treatment because it has shown no efficacy and is potentially harmful?

Options.text: Start supplemental oxygen via nasal cannula

CorrectAnswer: Start supplemental oxygen via nasal cannula
ExplanationEN: Current ACC/AHA recommendations state that patients with oxygen saturations of 90% or above should not be given supplemental oxygen unless they have obvious respiratory distress. Lack of benefit and possible harm from hyperoxia.
ExplanationAR: في NSTEMI مع SpO2 ≥90% بدون ضائقة تنفسية: لا يُعطى الأكسجين التكميلي روتينيًا (لا فائدة وقد يضر). أما الأسبرين والكلوبيدوغريل والهيبارين فهي علاجات موصى بها.
ClinicalScenario: A 61-year-old woman with HTN, T2DM, depression presents with 2 hours of substernal chest pressure. ECG unremarkable, troponin elevated. Concern for NSTEMI. Which intervention is no longer recommended in the initial treatment because it has shown no efficacy and is potentially harmful?
